name: browser-storage
description: Rules for localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies and IndexedDB in browser JavaScript. Thresholds here were calibrated against cmd/semlint/fixtures; see the README for the method before changing one.

rules.why: Browser storage throws in private mode, with cookies blocked, or when the origin is partitioned. An access that is not meaningfully guarded takes the whole feature down rather than degrading.

ask.instructions: In `code`, the marked line at `site_line` touches browser storage, which can throw. Check whether a try block already covers that line, in `code` or in `enclosing_scope`, including one opened many lines above it. If that call threw, would the surrounding feature break: an exception escaping to the caller, a handler stopping part way, or the element being left half-initialised? Answer no if the throw is caught and the code carries on sensibly, including a catch that deliberately does nothing.
ask.yes: A throw would break the feature or escape uncaught
ask.no: A throw is caught and the code continues in a sensible state

rules.message: browser storage access is not meaningfully guarded against throwing
rules._status: measured by -separation over three fixtures: ROBUST +0.69. Threshold sits in the middle of the robust gap.

rules.why: Anything in browser storage can be stale from an older version, corrupted, or written by other code on the same origin. Using it without checking its shape turns bad data into a runtime error.

ask.instructions: In `code`, a value is read from browser storage at `site_line`. Is that value then used in a way that assumes a shape or type nobody verified, such as indexing into it, calling a method on it, or passing it somewhere that requires a particular format? Answer no if it is only compared against a constant, checked for truthiness before structural use, or assigned somewhere that accepts any string.
ask.yes: The value is used as though its shape were guaranteed
ask.no: The value is checked, or only used in ways any string survives

rules.message: value read from storage is used without validating its shape
rules._status: measured by -separation over three fixtures: ROBUST +0.42. Threshold sits in the middle of the robust gap.

rules.why: A runtime library shares an origin with the host application. An un-namespaced key can collide with the application's own data and silently overwrite it.

ask.instructions: In `code`, look at the storage key used at `site_line`. Is it built without any library-specific prefix or namespace, so that a generic name could collide with a key another script on the same origin might use? If the key is built by a helper or constant, look it up in `module_scope_declarations` and judge what that produces. Answer no if the key includes a distinctive prefix, a constant naming the library or feature, or is otherwise clearly scoped.
ask.yes: The key is generic and could collide with another script's key
ask.no: The key carries a distinctive prefix or namespace

rules.message: storage key is not namespaced and may collide with host application data
rules._status: measured by -separation over three fixtures: ROBUST +0.85. Threshold sits in the middle of the robust gap.

rules.why: Browser storage is a small fixed budget shared with the host application. Keys written per item with no eviction eventually fill it and every write starts failing.

ask.instructions: In `code`, storage keys are written at `site_line`. Does this write create a new key per item, per id, or per session, in a way that accumulates without any code here removing old entries or bounding how many exist? Answer no if the key is one fixed name, or if this code removes old entries or caps how many are kept, including through a helper named in `module_scope_declarations`.
ask.yes: Keys accumulate without any bound or cleanup
ask.no: The key is fixed, or old entries are cleaned up here

rules.message: writes an unbounded set of storage keys with no eviction
rules._status: measured by -separation over three fixtures: ROBUST +0.59. Threshold sits in the middle of the robust gap.

rules.why: Browser storage is readable by any script on the origin and survives until cleared. Tokens, credentials, or personal data in it are exposed to any successful injection.

ask.instructions: In `code`, what is written to storage at `site_line`? Does it look like a credential, session token, API key, password, or personal information about a user? Answer no for interface state such as which tab is open, a theme, a dismissed notice, a draft the user typed, or scroll position.
ask.yes: It stores a credential, token, or personal information
ask.no: It stores interface state or user-visible content

rules.message: writes data to browser storage that looks sensitive
rules._status: measured by -separation over three fixtures: ROBUST +0.87. Threshold sits in the middle of the robust gap.

rules.why: When the read side and the write side build a key differently, the feature silently never finds what it stored. Nothing errors and no test catches it unless it asserts persistence. Split across two files, each side looks correct on its own.

ask.instructions: A storage key is built at `site_line`. Compare how it is built here with how the same key is built everywhere else it appears: check `other_matching_lines_in_file` for the rest of this file, and `related_lines_in_other_files` for lines in other files that share the same prefix constant or helper name. Does any other side apply a prefix or an encoding step that this one omits, or omit one that this one applies, so a value written under one spelling would never be found under the other? Answer no if every side builds the key identically or goes through the same helper, and no if no other side is shown to you.
ask.yes: Another side builds the same key differently, so writes and reads do not meet
ask.no: Every side shown builds the key the same way, or no other side is shown

rules.message: the read and write sides appear to build the storage key differently
rules._status: measured by -separation over three fixtures: ROBUST +0.78. Threshold sits in the middle of the robust gap. Extended to consult related lines in other files, which is the only way the split-across-modules version of this bug is visible.

rules.why: Storage is shared across tabs but a value cached in a variable is not. Without a storage event listener, two open tabs drift apart until one reloads.

ask.instructions: In `code`, a stored value is read at `site_line` and drives something the user sees. Would two tabs of the same site visibly disagree after one of them changed this value, because nothing listens for the storage event to pick up another tab's change? Check `enclosing_scope` as well as `code`: the listener is often installed by the function that wraps this one. Answer no if the value is re-read on each use, or if disagreement between tabs would not be noticeable.
ask.yes: Two open tabs would visibly disagree until one reloads
ask.no: The value is re-read on use, or divergence is not user-visible

rules.message: state read once from storage can diverge between open tabs
rules._status: measured by -separation over three fixtures: ROBUST +0.43. Threshold sits in the middle of the robust gap.

rules.why: clear() erases every key on the origin, including the host application's. A library has no business calling it; it should remove its own namespaced keys instead.
rules.message: clear() erases all storage for the origin, not just this library's keys

rules.why: JSON.parse throws on malformed input. Parsing anything that came from storage, a URL, or the network without a guard turns bad data into a broken page.

ask.instructions: In `code`, JSON.parse is called at `site_line`. Is its argument data that could be malformed, such as something read from browser storage, a URL, an attribute, or a network response, without the call being inside a try/catch or otherwise protected from throwing? Check `enclosing_scope` for a try block opened by the caller.
ask.yes: Possibly-malformed input is parsed with nothing catching a throw
ask.no: The input is known-good, or the parse is guarded

rules.message: JSON.parse on possibly-malformed input is not guarded
rules._status: measured by -separation over three fixtures: ROBUST +0.84. Threshold sits in the middle of the robust gap.

rules.why: A cookie written without SameSite is sent on cross-site requests, and one without an explicit path defaults to the current directory, so it is invisible on other pages.
rules.message: cookie is written without SameSite or without an explicit path

rules.why: An IndexedDB open without an upgrade handler fails on a fresh browser where the object stores do not exist yet, and an unhandled version change blocks later sessions.

ask.instructions: In `code`, IndexedDB is opened at `site_line`. Is the open missing an onupgradeneeded handler that creates the object stores it later uses, or missing an onerror or onblocked path, so a first run or a version change would leave it broken?
ask.yes: The upgrade or error path is missing
ask.no: Upgrade and failure paths are handled

rules.message: IndexedDB open is missing an upgrade or failure path
rules._status: measured by -separation over three fixtures: ROBUST +0.86. Threshold sits in the middle of the robust gap.
